entries.title: Venezuela earthquakes kill 920 people as families desperate for news
entries.snippet: Hundreds are still feared trapped under the rubble, as international rescue teams start to arrive.

entries.title: Mother dies saving daughter in Venezuela earthquakes
entries.snippet: Héctor Bello wrote on social media that "you gave your own life for our daughter" in the quakes which killed at least 920 people.

entries.title: US conducts strikes on Iran after attack on cargo ship
entries.snippet: US Central Command says it has struck missile and drone storage facilities and coastal radar positions.

entries.title: Europe's deadly heatwave breaks German record and halts public events
entries.snippet: Germany's highest ever temperature of 41.3C is recorded provisionally in Saarbrücken, over the border from France.

entries.title: DR Congo takes Rwanda to international court over decades of conflict
entries.snippet: Kinshasa accuses its neighbour of committing various violations since the 1994 Rwanda genocide.

entries.title: Israel and Lebanon sign framework agreement after US-brokered talks
entries.snippet: Hezbollah is not party to Friday's agreement, and previous ceasefires between Israel and Lebanon have still seen near-daily cross-border strikes.

entries.title: Ex-Trump adviser John Bolton pleads guilty to mishandling classified documents
entries.snippet: Bolton faces a prison sentence of up to five years and has agreed to pay $2.25m in fine, prosecutors say.

entries.title: Christmas market attacker jailed for life for murdering six in Germany
entries.snippet: A nine-year-old and five women were killed when Taleb Al-Abdulmohsen drove into the market in 2024.

entries.title: Senior Ukrainian intelligence official jailed for life for spying for Russia
entries.snippet: Col Dmytro Kozyura agreed to share state secrets and systematically disclosed classified information, prosecutors say.

entries.title: Four men held over child marriage in Sierra Leone appear in landmark court case
entries.snippet: It relates to a 17-year-old girl - four men including her father and husband face years in jail if convicted.

entries.title: Canada eligible to join Eurovision competition
entries.snippet: Prime Minister Mark Carney raised the idea of Canada joining the song contest in his 2025 budget.

entries.title: US sanctions Rwanda gold refinery accused of smuggling DR Congo's minerals
entries.snippet: The US alleges Gasabo Gold Refinery smuggled at least 60kg of gold in early 2026.

entries.title: Reflecting Pool liner cut with sharp knife or razor, National Park Service says
entries.snippet: Earlier in the week Donald Trump blamed vandals for "a 300 foot long gash" in the pool and accused someone of putting fertiliser in the water.

entries.title: Asia stock markets slide as tech shares slump
entries.snippet: Trading on South Korea's Kospi index was halted for the third time this week to prevent panic selling.

entries.title: Housing board votes to freeze New York rents in victory for Mamdani
entries.snippet: The decision was welcomed by many tenants - but landlords fear it will worsen housing conditions.

entries.title: Row over alleged theft of donations from India's landmark Ram temple
entries.snippet: Questions are being raised over the handling of cash, valuable jewellery, gold and silver offered by devotees.

entries.title: Paris restricts alcohol consumption and sales as Europe's heatwave shifts east
entries.snippet: Temperatures in Germany could hit 40C in some areas while French officials bring in alcohol restrictions to ease pressure on hospitals.

entries.title: Women alleging rape and sexual assault in France call to abolish statute of limitations
entries.snippet: More than 50 women are calling for the abolition of the statute of limitations which they say has prevented them seeking justice.

entries.title: Supreme Court allows Trump to end protected status for Haitian and Syrian immigrants
entries.snippet: The ruling opens the path for the Trump administration to deport hundreds of thousands of immigrants who have been living in the US for years.

entries.title: Trump asks Congress for billions for Iran war, after tension with Republicans
entries.snippet: But the budget faces an uphill battle as the president spars with some members of his own party over the issue.

entries.title: Pete Buttigieg and his kids subject to CPS, police investigation after false report
entries.snippet: Buttigieg, a potential 2028 Democratic presidential contender, shared his family's experience when police and Child Protective Services came to his home investigating an anonymous tip that was false.

entries.title: 5 million have dropped ACA insurance after Trump and the GOP let prices skyrocket
entries.snippet: The number of people who signed up for a health plan and then didn't pay their premium fell much more sharply than it has in years past. Trump officials blame fraud. Health policy experts blame costs.

entries.title: A day after Alito's testy response to Sotomayor's dissent, court says it was a 'misunderstanding'
entries.snippet: During Supreme Court opinions Thursday, Justice Samuel Alito, who wrote the majority opinion in an asylum case, appeared to rebut Justice Sonia Sotomayor, who wrote the dissent. The move was highly unusual — and on Friday there was a coda.

entries.title: It's not just Cape Verde: African soccer is having a World Cup moment
entries.snippet: The soccer greats — Brazil, England, Spain — have been giving uneven performances out on the pitch during this World Cup. Meanwhile, team from Africa have been relentless.

entries.title: She posted about ICE. Five months later, DHS agents told her to take her post down
entries.snippet: In January, Paigelynne Gonyea posted about the immigration surge in Minneapolis. This week, she was visited by ICE officials who claimed one of her posts had doxxed a federal agent.

entries.title: U.S. pledges generous earthquake relief to Venezuela
entries.snippet: Secretary of State Marco Rubio promised: "We have a whole-of-government response. It'll be big; it'll be fast; and it'll be effective."

entries.title: World Cup fans are missing games after their resale tickets fall through
entries.snippet: The ordeal has left fans forced to either miss out on a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity or scramble to find new tickets, often costing more and for worse seats.

entries.title: Palestinians grieve for a father-to-be shot by Israeli troops the day his son was born
entries.snippet: Nayef Samaro, 25, was killed in an Israeli military raid on Nablus, in the occupied West Bank, as he prepared to meet his wife at the hospital for the birth of their first child.

entries.title: Ukraine unleashes one of its heaviest drone bombardments, as Russia strikes Ukraine
entries.snippet: Ukraine launched a major nighttime attack on a dozen Russian regions, Russian-held Crimea and the surrounding seas, and Russia attacked various regions of Ukraine, as their war grinds on.

entries.title: Plane crashes into Beijing's tallest building; damage reported
entries.snippet: The cause of the damage could not be independently verified, and authorities did not immediately issue a statement on the incident.

entries.title: Apple increases prices for Macs and iPads, blaming memory chip shortage fueled by AI
entries.snippet: The Cupertino, California-based company called the demand spike an "unprecedented challenge" for the consumer electronics industry.

entries.title: Americans are inundated with suspected scams. New polls show why few victims report them
entries.snippet: Most Americans are inundated with scam attempts on a daily basis — and about 3 in 10 have personally lost money or personal information to scams, according to a new AP-NORC survey.

entries.title: DNC plans weekend of local events to focus on affordability concerns under Trump
entries.snippet: Two years ago, Democrats were the ones accused of being indifferent to Americans' anger about rising prices. Now they're pointing the finger at Trump, who has downplayed the impact of lingering inflation.

entries.title: Crews race to find survivors in mountains of rubble after Venezuela earthquakes

entries.title: WNBA suspends Alyssa Thomas for 1 game over hit to Caitlin Clark's throat
entries.snippet: The WNBA has suspended Phoenix's Alyssa Thomas for one game after she made contact with her fist to Caitlin Clark's throat in Wednesday night's matchup against Indiana.

entries.title: U.S. strikes Iran after drones target cargo ship in Strait of Hormuz
entries.snippet: On Friday, the U.S. military conducted new strikes against Iran in response to what President Trump said was Tehran's violation of the ceasefire. Nick Schifirin reports.

entries.snippet: Putin and Ivanov knew each other since the 1970s when they both worked as young KGB officers in their hometown of Leningrad, as St. Petersburg was called during the Soviet times.

entries.title: Why more school districts are limiting screen time for students
entries.snippet: The nation's second-largest school district imposed strict new limits on screen time for its roughly 400,000 students. The Los Angeles Unified School District policy is the latest example of a growing backlash against technology in classrooms nationwide. William Brangham discusse

entries.snippet: Heated games and rough plays sparked a new controversy in the WNBA around its superstar Caitlin Clark. The Phoenix Mercury's Alyssa Thomas pressed her fist into Clark's neck during a game. The league retroactively gave Thomas a flagrant foul and suspended her for one game. But qu

entries.title: Black Opera Project celebrates resilience and richness of the Black American experience

entries.title: U.S. strikes Iran in response to drone attack on cargo ship that Trump says violated ceasefire
entries.snippet: The strikes came shortly after Trump told reporters, "You'll find out," whether the U.S. would respond to a drone attack a day earlier on a cargo ship in the Strait of Hormuz.

entries.title: Texas education board approves Bible stories as required reading in public schools
entries.snippet: The Texas education board on Friday approved a required reading list for more than 5 million public school students that includes Bible passages, widening conservative efforts to push Christian teachings in U.S. classrooms.

entries.title: WATCH: Trump receives report from Religious Liberty Commission in the Oval Office
entries.snippet: A new report by a Trump administration commission suggests replacing the idea of separating church and state with the idea of building bridges between them.

entries.title: Live Results: Louisiana midterm primary runoffs
entries.snippet: Louisiana Republicans will nominate a candidate for U.S. Senate in a primary runoff Saturday, six weeks after denying Republican U.S. Sen. Bill Cassidy a shot at a third term.

entries.title: Newsom urges a national 'billionaires' tax' while fighting one in California
entries.snippet: The governor announced his agenda a day after an influential health care union in California pledged to go forward with a ballot measure that would impose a one-time 5% tax on the assets of billionaires living in the state as of Jan. 1, 2026. Newsom opposes that measure.

entries.title: Heat catches Europe's fashion industry unprepared as models face the sun in fur and wool
entries.snippet: The most coveted accessory at the Paris Fashion Week shows this week was not a bag, a sneaker or a watch. It was an ice pack.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Trump foe John Bolton pleads guilty in classified docs case
entries.snippet: Bolton faces as many as five years in prison. He had earlier served as Trump's national security adviser during the president's first term in office, but later resigned over his differences with Trump.

entries.title: US, Lebanon, Israel sign framework agreement
entries.snippet: US Secretary ‌of ⁠State ⁠Marco ​Rubio has announced ​a trilateral ​framework ‌agreement. Lebanese officials began direct talks with Israel in Washington in April.

entries.title: Creative climate messaging and other eco wins of the week
entries.snippet: An artist in Mali and climate scientists in the US are finding new ways to inform the public about the climate crisis.

entries.title: Fact check: throwing cold water on heat wave disinformation
entries.snippet: An outdated air-conditioning law, a viral health myth about sleeping with the fan on and the age-old climate change hoax allegation: DW checked what's spreading in Europe's heat wave.

entries.title: World Cup: Morocco's Ismael Saibari set for Bayern Munich
entries.snippet: Three nationalities, five languages and soon to be resident in a fourth country: Ismael Saibari, the star of Morocco's World Cup so far, is set to join Bayern Munich. But he has business to finish with the Atlas Lions.

entries.title: Comedy legend Mel Brooks turns 100
entries.snippet: His parody of Hitler in the landmark 1968 movie "The Producers" was just the beginning for US actor Mel Brooks. The 100-year-old comedian is still on a roll.

entries.title: German lawyers: Ban on far-right AfD 'likely successful'
entries.snippet: A new report by legal experts has found that efforts to ban Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) could be successful — but there would be political dangers to such a move.

entries.title: 'Operation Purgatory': Magyar moves to demolish Orban system
entries.snippet: The new Hungarian government is moving swiftly to dismantle the system of former PM Viktor Orban. The focus is on fighting corruption, reforming the media and protecting democracy.

entries.title: How the Iran war impacts Abu Dhabi's AI strategy
entries.snippet: Abu Dhabi's ambitions to turn the UAE into a global hub for digital infrastructure and AI, dubbed "UAE AI Strategy 2031," face pressure after the war with Iran. But the UAE is also known for its business resilience.

entries.title: World Cup: 'Pride Match' sparks objections in Egypt and Iran
entries.snippet: Friday night's game in Seattle was designated as a "Pride Match" well ahead of the World Cup draw. The fixture list then threw up Egypt vs. Iran, two countries in which homosexuality is criminalized.

entries.title: India news: Government sends help to quake-hit Venezuela
entries.snippet: Two air force planes carrying supplies as well as a field hospital unit are on their way. Also making headlines: Qatar has repatriated the bodies of four Indians killed in a gas explosion. DW has more.

entries.title: Wagner festival reinstates Holocaust memorial event after cancellation
entries.snippet: The Bayreuth Festival had canceled a planned memorial lecture featuring Jewish author and broadcaster Michel Friedman, drawing sharp criticism.

entries.title: Bayer: Why so many Roundup weedkiller lawsuits?
entries.snippet: Bayer was sued for failing to add cancer warnings to its controversial pesticide Roundup when US regulators opposed adding one. DW asks if the latest Supreme Court win will shield the chemical giant from paying billions.

entries.title: Balochistan activist's life sentence raises fear of unrest
entries.snippet: With the conviction of a leading rights campaigner, Pakistan has drawn criticism from rights groups and sparked fears it could deepen unrest in Balochistan and weaken trust in peaceful activism.

entries.title: Flights disrupted in Japan as 2 tropical storms move in
entries.snippet: Two storms were set to converge above Japan, prompting officials to issue landslide warnings and evacuation orders for hundreds of thousands of people.

entries.title: Japan needs more foreign workers, but many feel unwelcome
entries.snippet: While Japan faces a deepening labor shortage and growing demand for foreign workers, it has been moving to tighten visa rules and regulations.

entries.title: Montenegro arrests Iran-linked hacker wanted by US
entries.snippet: The FBI was helping the Montenegrin police detain an Iranian-Turkish national whose cyberattacks on US infrastructure allegedly caused billions in damages.

entries.title: Fact check: As Europe bakes, should you trust your sunscreen?
entries.snippet: As a heatwave sweeps across Europe, claims are resurfacing online questioning whether sunscreen is safe or linked to skin cancer risk.

entries.title: Sudan: Fears of atrocities as RSF surrounds key city
entries.snippet: As Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces mass around the strategic city of el-Obeid, fears are growing of atrocities similar to those seen in Darfur's el-Fasher. Could sanctions still prevent bloodshed?
